sources.text: Given two integers x and y, return their sum. No state or external effects are permitted.
sources.concern: Pure relation; no invented invalid-input policy.

sources.text: Create a note with a caller-supplied unique key and text. Reading that key returns its text. Updating that key replaces only its text. Deleting that key makes it absent. Other notes remain unchanged. Behavior for absent or duplicate keys is unspecified.
sources.concern: CRUD composition and frame conditions; explicit partial domain.

sources.text: Given a sequence of records with name and active fields, return exactly the active records, sorted by name in ascending Unicode code-point order. Equal names retain their input order. Do not change the input.
sources.concern: Selection, exact cardinality, total ordering and stable ties.

sources.text: Given an ASCII string, remove leading and trailing ASCII space characters and convert A through Z to a through z; return the result. Internal spaces are unchanged.
sources.concern: Precisely bounded normalization and transformation composition.

sources.text: A ticket starts OPEN. Closing an OPEN ticket changes it to CLOSED and returns CLOSED. Closing a CLOSED ticket returns ALREADY_CLOSED and changes no state. No other ticket changes. Tickets must always be OPEN or CLOSED.
sources.concern: Conditional transition, invariant, error and frame.

sources.text: Store a supplied integer under a supplied key. A later read of that key, including after process restart, returns the last successfully stored integer. If storage fails, return STORAGE_ERROR and preserve all previously readable values. The storage engine is not prescribed.
sources.concern: Persistence, failure atomicity and implementation neutrality.

sources.text: Given an object with an optional nullable integer value, return ABSENT when value is omitted, NULL when it is explicitly null, and that integer otherwise. Return INVALID for any other present value. Produce no state changes or external effects.
sources.concern: Omission versus null, exact input rejection.
Material ambiguity without an ordering definition.

sources.text: For every input sequence of names, return all names in insertion order and always sorted alphabetically ascending.
For a positive integer n, return n plus one.
sources.concern: Success-only domain; invalid inputs and effects unspecified.

sources.text: Given a sequence of integers and a nonnegative integer limit, return at most limit positive values in their original order, taking the earliest qualifying values. Return an empty sequence when limit is zero. Do not mutate the input.
sources.concern: Compositional selection, cardinality, prefix and conditional behavior.

sources.text: On an accepted reservation, reduce available seats by the requested positive count and return the remaining count. Accept only when the requested count does not exceed available seats. Otherwise return INSUFFICIENT and change nothing. Available seats must never be negative. Emit exactly one confirmation to the caller on success and none on rejection.
sources.concern: Pre/postconditions, invariant, externally observable effects and exact counts.

public_example.policy: Already public; original source remains unchanged. Requirement-local scope, not an imported baseline contract.
